cosy-lesson.title: My Life With & My Life Without Fast Food (B1)

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Convenience ≠ hassle – the state of being useful, easy, or quick to do.

p.em: Example: Fast food offers unparalleled convenience during busy workdays.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nutrition ≠ junk – the process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for health.

p.em: Example: Balancing convenience with proper nutrition is a challenge.

cosy-blockquote.p: Processing ≠ fresh – the alteration of food items from their natural state.

p.em: Example: Ultra-processed foods often contain excess sodium and preservatives.

cosy-blockquote.p: Affordability ≠ expense – the ability to be bought without costing too much money.

p.em: Example: The affordability of fast food attracts budget-conscious students.

cosy-blockquote.p: Craving ≠ aversion – a powerful desire for something, especially food.

p.em: Example: Late-night fast food cravings are driven by high sugar and fat content.

cosy-blockquote.p: Calorie ≠ empty – a unit of energy in food.

p.em: Example: Fast food meals can contain an entire day's recommended calorie intake.

cosy-blockquote.p: Addictive ≠ wholesome – causing a strong, compulsive reliance.

p.em: Example: Combination of salt and fats makes fast food highly addictive.

cosy-blockquote.p: Moderation ≠ excess – the avoidance of excess or extremes.

p.em: Example: Enjoying fast food in moderation poses fewer health risks.

cosy-blockquote.p: Substitutes ≠ originals – a person or thing acting in place of another.

p.em: Example: Healthy fast-casual bowls are popular substitutes for burgers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Obesity ≠ wellness – the state of being grossly overweight.

p.em: Example: High fast food consumption is linked to rising rates of obesity.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why is the convenience of quick takeaway food so appealing to busy modern workers?
★ How often do you order fast food during busy weeks?

How does high-calorie fast food lack essential nutrition compared to home-cooked meals?
★ Do you pay attention to vitamins and micronutrients in your food?

What industrial processing methods are used in factory-prepared meals?
★ Are you concerned about artificial preservatives in packaged food?

How does the low cost and affordability of fast food drive consumer choices?
★ Is eating healthy food expensive in your city?

How do targeted food advertisements trigger an intense junk food craving?
★ What fast food dish do you crave most often?

Why is understanding empty calorie density important for maintaining health?
★ Do you count daily calories when trying to manage weight?

What makes ultra-processed foods highly addictive for young children?
★ Was fast food a special treat during your childhood?

How can practicing dietary moderation allow people to enjoy fast food occasionally without guilt?
★ How do you balance healthy meals with treats?

What healthy plant-based substitutes can replace fast food burgers?
★ Have you tried plant-based fast food options?

How does reducing fast food intake prevent metabolic diseases and obesity?
★ What positive health changes did you notice after cooking at home more?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
The sheer convenience of fast food outweighs its nutritional drawbacks for busy families. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you cook every day if you had more free time?

Public schools should eliminate all fast food options to guarantee proper student nutrition. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Were school meals healthy in your youth?

Heavy industrial processing makes commercial fast food harmful to human health. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Avoid processed foods when shopping?

The high affordability of fast food makes it the only accessible option for low-income families. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should healthy organic food be subsidized by governments?

Resisting a strong sugar or salt craving is a matter of self-discipline and awareness. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you overcome late-night snack cravings?

Food packaging should display clear warning labels showing total calorie count. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should high-calorie foods carry warning labels like cigarettes?

Fast food recipes are scientifically engineered to be hyper-palatable and addictive. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Believe fast food companies exploit human brain biology?

Enjoying fast food in strict moderation is completely compatible with a healthy lifestyle. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you allow yourself weekly cheat meals?

Creating tasty home substitutes for fast food is easier than most people think. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you make homemade burgers or pizza?

Combating rising childhood obesity requires taxing high-sugar fast food items heavily. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Support sugar and fast food taxes?

ul.li: Incorrect: Despite it is cheap, it is unhealthy. → Correct: Despite its low cost / Although it is cheap, it is unhealthy. (('Despite' requires a noun phrase or gerund, not a subject-verb clause.))
Incorrect: Fast food makes me to feel tired. → Correct: Fast food makes me feel tired. ((The verb 'make' in causative sense takes a bare infinitive: 'make me feel'.))
